name: Tine
description: Modelled tine electric piano: struck tines and tone bars read by a pickup that barks when played hard, through a suitcase amplifier with stereo tremolo.

params.name: Bell
params.description: How much of the high bell tone rings at the start of each note. Applies from the next note played.

params.name: Bark
params.description: Moves the tine closer to the pickup. Low is hollow and pure; high growls on hard notes while soft notes stay clean.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long held notes ring. Bass notes always last longer than treble. Applies from the next note played.

params.name: Release
params.description: How quickly the damper stops a note after the key is let go. Short is tight; long lets notes hang over.

params.name: Hardness
params.description: How much playing harder changes the tone as well as the loudness. At zero a hard note is a loud soft note.

params.name: Tremolo
params.description: Depth of the suitcase amplifier's tremolo. Loudness stays the same as the depth goes up.

params.name: Rate
params.description: How fast the tremolo pulses, or pans when Pan is up.

params.name: Pan
params.description: Spreads the tremolo across the speakers. At zero both sides pulse together; at full the sound swings from side to side.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Amplifier tone control. Low settings are dark and muffled; high settings let the bell and bark through.

params.name: Drive
params.description: How hard the notes push the amplifier. Quiet playing stays clean; loud notes and chords saturate and compress.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. Pushed hard, a soft clipper rounds off the peaks.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A signal model in the manner of the tine electric pianos of the seventies (a struck tine with a short inharmonic second mode, a tone bar that carries the sustain, an electromagnetic pickup modelled as the rate of change of a bell-shaped flux curve, a suitcase-style stereo tremolo); it uses no samples and is not a circuit model of any one instrument.
